implementerProof.how: Round 4's own proof for the new memory paragraph does not hold on the surface it names. The paragraph, and the proof behind it, cite `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current` with exact byte figures; that file does not exist in a role container of this pod. Measured in my tester container at head 06e272bf7d46ee94b70bca1c32d97f7553ec9e3e: `/sys/fs/cgroup` carries cgroup v1 controllers only (cpu, cpuacct, cpuset, devices, job, memory, pids), `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/` holds `memory.usage_in_bytes` and `memory.limit_in_bytes` and no `memory.current`, and `find /sys/fs/cgroup -maxdepth 3 -name memory.current` prints nothing. Asked the implementer, which reproduced the same absence in its own container and answered (Envoy, 2026-10-21T00:49:29Z) that its command was `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current 2>/dev/null || cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes`, the fallback fired silently, and the figures are v1 `memory.usage_in_bytes` readings carrying a v2 file name. The paragraph's substance does reproduce — a tmpfs write is resident memory — and everything else in round 4's diff is verified below, so the rejection is this paragraph alone. The rest of round 4 answers review round 1 correctly: the Evidence attribution now matches dispatch://INFRA-51/comment/0ce1448c-ccbc-4b5f-aaaf-60dce4c5eb05 word for word (planner container, 22:20Z, devices 83/56/97/87, `du -sx /` 42 MB), and `sjawhar/legion#2088` is in `related_issues`.

failures.evidence: docs/solutions/testing/a-pod-harness-moves-tmpdir-too-and-the-failure-mode-is-a-silent-kill-INFRA-44.md:57-66 says a `dd bs=1M count=100` into `/var/run/legion/private` 'moved `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current` from 766,550,016 to 871,407,616 bytes' and that 'a second role container of the same pod read 708,227,072 → 813,051,904'. Measured in the INFRA-69 tester container at head 06e272bf7d46ee94b70bca1c32d97f7553ec9e3e: `ls -l /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current` → 'No such file or directory'; `ls /sys/fs/cgroup` → cpu, cpuacct, cpuset, devices, job, memory, pids (cgroup v1, as `/proc/mounts` shows: `none /sys/fs/cgroup/memory cgroup rw,memory`); `ls /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/` → cgroup.procs, memory.limit_in_bytes, memory.move_charge_at_immigrate, memory.pressure_level, memory.soft_limit_in_bytes, memory.usage_in_bytes, tasks; `find /sys/fs/cgroup -maxdepth 3 -name memory.current` → nothing. The implementer ran the same three commands in its own container and got the same absence, and reported that its measurement command was `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current 2>/dev/null || cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes`, whose silent fallback produced the figures (Envoy, 2026-10-21T00:49:29Z). So a reader following the paragraph gets 'No such file or directory'. What does reproduce, measured here: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes` 711,213,056 → 816,320,512 bytes around the 100 MiB `dd` into `/var/run/legion/private`, and `free -k` shared 132 → 102,532 KiB — exactly the 102,400 KiB written — falling back to 132 KiB when the file is removed; the implementer read 777,203,712 → 881,893,376 and the same 132 → 102,532 KiB shared in its container. Fix: write the v1 path this runtime actually has (`/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes`), or make `free -k`'s `shared` column the measurement, which is exact in all three containers and independent of the cgroup layout; if the paragraph names `memory.current` at all it must say it is the cgroup v2 path a reader's own cluster may have and this pod does not. No repository test pins it: there is no checker over docs/solutions/ prose and a grep over wording is a source-text test the conventions forbid; the four commands above are the re-runnable evidence.

failures.criterion: BLOCKING. The note claims only what its measurement can show (spec acceptance 1): the cgroup counter those figures come from is the gVisor sandbox's, not the container's, so it cannot demonstrate the per-container charging the paragraph asserts with it.
failures.evidence: The paragraph says a write to one of the in-memory emptyDirs 'is charged against the container's **memory** limit' and carries that claim on the byte figures above. The counter a role container can read is sandbox-wide: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes` reads 20,401,094,656 bytes in my tester container and the same 20,401,094,656 in the implementer's, which equals `free -k`'s total of 19,922,944 KiB and is neither the 6Gi the golden pod JSON gives the tester and implementer nor the 1Gi it gives the architect, planner and merger (packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/testdata/golden/root.json; defaultResources, packages/daemon/internal/config/kubernetes.go:179-186). Three readings taken minutes apart in three different containers — 766,550,016 (implementer), 708,227,072 (reviewer), 711,213,056 (tester) — are one magnitude, which is what a single shared counter looks like and not what three per-container counters would look like. The implementer agrees (Envoy, 2026-10-21T00:49:29Z): 'that is the gVisor sandbox's cgroup, not the Kubernetes per-container limit'. Per-container charging of tmpfs pages is true as Kubernetes platform behaviour, but nothing inside this pod demonstrates it, and this note's whole subject is the difference between what was measured and what was assumed. Fix: state what the measurement shows — a tmpfs write is resident memory for as long as the file exists, with the `free -k` shared figures and the sandbox-wide scope of the counter named — and either attribute the per-container charging to Kubernetes' own documented behaviour or leave it out, the way the TMPDIR bullet now attributes INFRA-44's staging rather than claiming it here. The per-role limits from defaultResources are verified and may stay as the configured limits they are.

failures.criterion: Minor. The final paragraph's support for 'no API server' misstates what its cited live assertion asserts.
failures.evidence: The note's closing paragraph (:171-178) says 'The pod sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and names no ServiceAccount of its own (… golden/root.json; the live assertion is in … live_operator_test.go)'. The golden fixture does carry `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and no `serviceAccountName`, but live_operator_test.go:44-49 asserts the opposite of the second half: it refuses a pod whose `ServiceAccountName` is not the operator's (`pod.Spec.ServiceAccountName != r.pod.ServiceAccount`) and whose `AutomountServiceAccountToken` is nil or true, and its note line reads 'pod %s: serviceAccountName %s, automountServiceAccountToken false'. So in the live deployment the pod does run under a ServiceAccount — the operator's — and the reason nothing inside reaches the API server is the unmounted token, not an absent ServiceAccount. The reader-facing conclusion is verified and unaffected: `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io` does not exist and `kubectl get --raw /api` answers 'The connection to the server localhost:8080 was refused - did you specify the right host or port?', exactly as the note says. Fix: drop 'and names no ServiceAccount of its own', or write 'runs under the operator's ServiceAccount with no token mounted'.
